message.content:
In this repository, find where "memo" objects have derived/computed metadata (e.g., title, excerpt/preview, word count, reading time, plain text extraction) that is computed automatically from the memo's content rather than set directly by the user.

Specifically answer:
1. Where (file path + function/method name) is this derived metadata computed?
2. What operations/events trigger the recomputation (e.g., on create, on update/save, before save hook, API endpoint)?
3. What specific properties/fields does the computation extract or derive (e.g., title, excerpt, word count, etc.)?

Search for "memo" model/schema files, look for hooks like beforeSave, pre-save middleware, computed properties, or service functions that process memo content. Check for words like "excerpt", "preview", "title", "wordCount", "summary" near memo-related code.

Report back with exact file paths and line numbers, and quote the relevant code.

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

content.text:
I have all the pieces needed now. This is the usememos/memos Go backend (this is the "memos" note-taking app, whose data model is called "memo").

## Summary

**1. Where is derived metadata computed?**

- **`/bench/repo/internal/markdown/markdown.go`** — the `markdown.Service` interface (goldmark-based) does the actual extraction:
  - `ExtractAll(content []byte) (*ExtractedData, error)` — line 356 — single-pass extraction of tags, mentions, and properties (including title).
  - `ExtractProperties(content []byte) (*storepb.MemoPayload_Property, error)` — line 193 — computes `HasLink`, `HasCode`, `HasTaskList`, `HasIncompleteTasks`, and `Title` (extracted from a leading H1 heading via `extractHeadingText`, line 173).
  - `ExtractTags` — line 143 — walks the AST for `#tag` nodes.
  - `GenerateSnippet(content []byte, maxLength int) (string, error)` — line 264 — walks the markdown AST to build a plain-text excerpt/preview, skipping code blocks.

- **`/bench/repo/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go`** — `RebuildMemoPayload(_ context.Context, memo *store.Memo, markdownService markdown.Service) error` (line 74). This is the "save hook" equivalent: it calls `markdownService.ExtractAll(...)` and assigns the results onto `memo.Payload.Tags` and `memo.Payload.Property` (which contains `Title`, `HasLink`, `HasCode`, `HasTaskList`, `HasIncompleteTasks`).

- **`/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go:83`** — `(s *APIV1Service) getMemoContentSnippet(content string)` — a thin wrapper calling `MarkdownService.GenerateSnippet([]byte(content), 64)` to produce a 64-char plain-text excerpt on demand.

- **`/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_converter.go:76`** (also 225, 248) — `convertMemoFromStoreWithCreators` computes `memoMessage.Snippet` by calling `getMemoContentSnippet(memo.Content)` every time a memo is converted from the store model to the API response model (i.e., computed on read, not persisted).

**2. What triggers recomputation?**

- **On create**: `CreateMemo` in `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:108` calls `memopayload.RebuildMemoPayload(ctx, create, s.MarkdownService)` before `s.Store.CreateMemo(...)`.
- **On update (only when content changes)**: `UpdateMemo`, same file, line 447, inside the loop over `request.UpdateMask.Paths` — only when `path == "content"` — calls `RebuildMemoPayload` again and sets `update.Payload = memo.Payload`.
- **Batch/background rebuild**: `Runner.RunOnce(ctx)` in `memopayload/runner.go:27` — iterates all memos in pages of 100 and calls `RebuildMemoPayload` + `Store.UpdateMemo` for each; used as a maintenance/migration job to backfill/refresh payloads for existing memos.
- **Snippet is not persisted at all** — it's recomputed every time a memo is serialized to the API response (`convertMemoFromStoreWithCreators`), when listing related-memo previews (`memo_relation_service.go:154,162`), and when building notification/webhook payloads (`user_service_notifications.go:323`).
- **Mentions** are re-extracted on demand via `MarkdownService.ExtractAll` in `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_mention_helpers.go:32` (used for @mention notifications).

**3. What fields are derived?**

From `storepb.MemoPayload_Property` (persisted in `memo.Payload`, proto at `/bench/repo/proto/gen/store/memo.pb.go`):
- `Title` — string, extracted from the first-block H1 heading if present (`extractHeadingText`).
- `HasLink` — bool, set if any markdown link node is found.
- `HasCode` — bool, set if any code block/fenced code block/code span is found.
- `HasTaskList` / `HasIncompleteTasks` — bool, set from GFM task-list checkboxes.
- `Tags` — `[]string`, all `#tag` occurrences (deduplicated, case-preserving), stored on `memo.Payload.Tags`.

Computed but **not persisted** (regenerated on every read/response):
- `Snippet` — plain-text excerpt/preview (max 64 chars for most call sites), used in list views, memo-relation previews, notifications, and webhook payloads.
- `Mentions` — `[]string` of lowercased usernames from `@mention` nodes, used transiently to drive mention notifications (not stored on the memo itself).

No explicit "word count" or "reading time" field exists in this codebase — the closest analogs are `Title`, `Tags`, boolean `Property` flags, and the `Snippet` excerpt.
